results.title: With new law, Iraq sees rise in child marriage, custody battles
results.content: In January 2025, Iraq's parliament passed an amendment allowing families to place their household under religious law, governing all issues around marriage, divorce and inheritance. The new Ja'fari law, a Shiite law, came into force in October 2025. One year on, its consequences have been raising serious alarm, especially among women, who say they've seen a major rollback of their rights. FRANCE 24's Marie-Charlotte Roupie reports, with Josh Vardey.

results.title: Japan's radical past: Retracing the far-left groups of the 1970s
results.content: Our correspondents delve into the history of Japan's radical left in the 1970s. From the United Red Army to the Japanese Red Army, several movements turned to armed struggle and violent action. More than half a century on, our team met with two former militants.

results.title: US: Thanksgiving storms cause flooding and travel chaos
results.content: Severe storms battered the US East Coast on Thursday, bringing torrential rain, strong winds and coastal flooding. Nearly one million homes were left without power, while hundreds of flights were cancelled and thousands delayed during one of the country's busiest travel periods. The weather also forced the postponement of New York's Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade until Saturday.

results.title: Black Friday: The evolution of a shopping phenomenon
results.content: Once defined by crowds queuing outside shops for one-off bargains, Black Friday has evolved into weeks of online promotions. As discounts spread throughout the year, consumers are becoming more cautious about advertised deals, increasingly turning to AI and price comparisons to find genuine bargains. Camille Knight looks at the origins of the global shopping phenomenon.

results.title: Ukraine: Residents brace for another difficult winter
results.content: As Russia continues to target Ukraine's energy infrastructure, residents are preparing for another difficult winter of strikes and power cuts. With supply chains under pressure, food prices are also rising, forcing many Ukrainians to cut back on essentials or stock up ahead of the coming months.

results.title: Spain election: Housing crisis and immigration dominate final campaign debate
results.content: Spain goes to the polls on Sunday in an early parliamentary election that may usher in a right-wing coalition to replace the Socialist-led minority government of Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, one of Europe's last leftist leaders. Our correspondent Sarah Morris tells us more.

results.title: Kuwait: Two Italians killed in drone attack
results.content: A drone attack in Kuwait killed two Italian technicians working on an air defence system on Thursday, marking the first fatal strike in the Gulf state for months.

results.title: EU: Leaders fail to reach agreement on next budget after tense summit
results.content: At the bloc headquarters in Brussels on Thursday, EU leaders failed to reach a consensus after more than 12 hours of talks over the budget and a new $49 billion loan for Ukraine’s economic and military needs next year. France 24's Dave Keating tells us more.

results.title: Israel's Eisenkot reaches deal with left-wing faction as coalition talks gain steam
results.content: Gadi ​Eisenkot's Yashar party and a left-wing faction agreed on a preliminary coalition deal on Thursday, after a brief dispute that had posed a challenge to his bid to unseat Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu following an inconclusive election last month. France 24's Andrew Hilliar tells us more.

results.title: Immigration: South Africa no longer an El Dorado for foreigners
results.content: South Africa was once a welcoming country; a refuge for those fleeing conflict and persecution. But for thousands of foreigners, the dream of a new life in South Africa is turning into more of a nightmare. Against a backdrop of unemployment and economic hardship, anti-immigration movements are gaining ground. Our correspondents report.

results.title: Spain’s Pedro makes final campaign push to beat the right ahead of crunch vote
results.content: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez holds a final rally in Madrid on Friday, the last day of campaigning for Sunday's high-stakes elections. Opinion polls show the Socialist premier lagging behind the main right-wing Popular Party (PP) as the Spanish vote opens an electoral cycle over the next 12 months that could reshape the balance of power within the EU.

results.title: Israel's Eisenkot and left-wing party agree coalition deal
results.content: The centrist party of Gadi Eisenkot, who is trying to form the next Israeli government, and an allied left-wing party on Thursday announced they had agreed on a coalition deal.

results.title: Spain general election 2026: Could Sánchez lose power?
results.content: Spanish voters head to the polls in just three days for a snap election, after eight years of Socialist-led rule. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez is fighting to stay in power, but an alliance between the conservative People's Party and the far-right VOX could bring his time in office to an end. So what are the key issues, and what's at stake?

results.title: EU leaders split over budget spending and a $49 billion loan to Ukraine
results.content: French President Emmanuel Macron set an end-of-year deadline for an agreement on the European Union's next seven-year budget after the continent's leaders ruled out any chances for a deal to be reached at their summit on Thursday.

results.title: Live: Trump calls on Putin to end all 'military aggression' against Europe
results.content: US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that he had urged his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin to "pull back all military aggression against territories throughout Europe". Although Trump did not provide any further details, he added that he hoped this would pave the way for a peace deal to be struck between Kyiv and Moscow. Follow our liveblog for all the latest updates.

results.title: Why is India so afraid of Pakistan's new Netflix series?
results.content: PRESS REVIEW – Friday, November 27: Controversy brews as India asks Netflix to ban a Pakistani series from being broadcast in the country. Tensions have been high between the two nations since last year's terror attack in the Kashmir region. Also in the news: Taiwanese voters will head to the polls for all-important local elections overshadowed by the threat of Chinese claims to the island. Finally, forget schadenfreude – practicing "freudenfreude" is better for your health.

results.title: Five people hospitalised as Levski Sofia and Marseille fans clash ahead of Europa League game
results.content: Fighting broke out ahead of Thursday's Europa League match between Levski Sofia and Olympique Marseille, with five Bulgarian fans ending up in hospital. Local media reported a number of Levski fans performing Nazi salutes in the lead-up to the skirmish.

results.title: France and Germany push for EU budget deal by year-end as far-right rise threatens Ukraine aid
results.content: As Europe braces itself for a slew of tense elections in 2027, Paris and Berlin are pushing for the European Union to strike a budget deal by December 31 to lock in financial aid for Ukraine. But Thursday's talks in Brussels seem to have done little to build consensus around the bloc's next budget.

results.title: 'Tribal loyalty' works on right: 'Heart on the left' sensitive to racism, anti-Semitism
results.content: As French far-right leader Jordan Bardella denies fresh allegations concerning anti-Semitic remarks he allegedly made as a teenager, how much damage could the affair do to Marine Le Pen's presidential prospects? Ana Navarro Pedro, correspondent for Portuguese media, believes its electoral impact may be limited, despite Le Pen's defence of Bardella and her choice of him as a future prime minister. "What they most regret in this whole episode is that Bardella is denying it," she says of prospective Le Pen voters.

results.title: Almost a million Americans left without power on Thanksgiving as storm sweeps East Coast
results.content: Nearly a million people were left without power Thursday after a severe storm lashed the East Coast of the US, tearing up trees and powerlines on Thanksgiving. New York City authorities had been forced to postpone the annual Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade due to the intense winds.

results.title: Israel's Eisenkot agrees to coalition deal with left-wing Democrats
results.content: Israel's former military chief Gadi Eisenkot on Thursday struck a coalition deal with Yair Golan's left-leaning Democrats, bringing the country's opposition closer to forming a government after no single bloc secured a majority in the October elections.

results.title: Lyon held and Marseille pushed in mixed Europa League night for French clubs
results.content: There were mixed fortunes for the French clubs in Thursday's Europa League action, as Marseille saw off Levski Sofia (1-0) in the only win of the night. Lyon were held at home by Lillestrom of Norway, while Rennes fell to Dutch side Nijmegen.

results.title: Black Friday hype stems from a desire 'to be part of a collective event', expert says
results.content: Once a strictly US affair, it's become a truly global phenomenon. From shoppers hunting for bargains in Louisiana, to queues forming outside stores in Venezuela, the Black Friday sales event has become the biggest day of the year for retail foot traffic. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Olaya Moldes Andres, Associate Professor in Marketing and Strategy at Cardiff Business School. She explains that, beyond the sales, the success of Black Friday may also be due to a desire by shoppers to "join the collective action. Whether it is spending money or going to the mall, shoppers feel part of a collective event, so perhaps this is where the whole hype comes from, to feel that we're being part of something, same thing as Christmas or any other social event".

results.title: RN’s antisemitic past ‘coming back to haunt them’: Will Le Pen ‘distance herself’ from Bardella?
results.content: Could new allegations of antisemitism damage Jordan Bardella’s standing and the far-right National Rally’s electoral prospects? Charli James is pleased to welcome Paul Smith, Associate Professor in French and Francophone Studies at the University of Nottingham. Smith examines the far-right leader’s continued denials and considers whether Marine Le Pen might eventually distance herself from him. In the meantime, Smith suggests that Bardella needs to “make his mind up” about how to respond to these latest troubling allegations published by Le Monde and Mediapart. “It’s very difficult to deny. Le Monde and Mediapart, certainly Le Monde, wouldn’t be publishing these details if they didn’t have some pretty substantial evidence.” Could this prove to be the Achilles’ heel of a far-right party with its sights set on the second round of the presidential election?
